newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia apple, pear industry welcomes NZ ban.
newsitem.headline: Australia apple, pear industry welcomes NZ ban.

text.p: The Australian apple and pear industry on Monday welcomed a foreshadowed decision by the Australian Quarantine and Inspection Service (AQIS) to reject access by New Zealand apples to the Australian market.

Australian Apple and Pear Growers' Association (AAPGA) chairman Jon Durham said in a statement that an AQIS draft analysis supported the industry's view that New Zealand could not guarantee apples free of the fire blight bacterial disease.

"We are one of the few countries in the world free of horticulture's foot and mouth disease and it is predicted that the introduction of the disease would cost A$922 million over six years through lost apple and pear production," he said.

AQIS said in a statement that its analysis had found that apples sourced under the New Zealand proposal for entry could carry fire blight bacteria and that the claim that apples could not act as a vector for the disease was unproven.
A spokesman said the analysis was now open to public consultation until June 13 but, unless any substantial issues arose, the service intended to reject the New Zealand request for access.
